newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-FINN, GREEK MAY COMPETE IN ATHENS DESPITE BANS.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-FINN, GREEK MAY COMPETE IN ATHENS DESPITE BANS.

text.p: Finnish runner Monica Kinnunen and Greek pole vaulter Stavros Tsitouras, presently serving drug bans, could compete at the world athletics championships if the IAAF changes its rules on doping this week.
Kinnunen, a 1,500 metres competitor, should miss the championships starting on Saturday because of a recent three-month ban for taking stimulants.
Tsitouras has served more than three years of a four-year ban for serious drug abuse.

But the International Amateur Athletic Federation said on Monday that the pair will be allowed to compete if the IAAF's congress, meeting on Wednesday and Thursday, decides to cut its compulsory bans for serious drugs from four to two years and to abandon suspensions for stimulants and just give athletes a serious warning.
It is widely believed that the congress will reduce the four-year ban because it has been found to be illegal under the civil law of many countries.
A ban of four years is regarded as too harsh under restraint of trade legislation and athletes could therefore go to court with a chance of winning their cases.
